name: Enoch
description: Man living at the time before the Flood

points: Cain knew his wife, and he builded a city. If Cain was the only child left, why would he need to build a city? There were thousands upon thousands of people already on the earth. He named the city after his son Enoch.

“And Cain knew his wife.” Why his wife? Because there was an abundance of people; that’s where his wife came from. Adam and Eve had a whole bunch of children. “And she conceived, and bare Enoch”: she bare a child named Enoch. “And he builded a city”: not for one family, for a multitude of people. “And called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.” So Cain built the city in the land of Nod, eastward of the garden where he used to be, and named it Enoch after his son.

Why would Cain name his son Enoch, such a weird name? That name sounds very familiar. The books bring it out: Cain’s Enoch has been identified with a fabulous king of the Babylonians, and the city Enoch with Erech. The Cainites, Cain’s descendants, dwelt in Enoch, or Erech. It was called Enoch first; later on Nimrod came over there, went to the same spot, and named it Erech, which is Iraq, which is Babylon.

points: In an old inscription, the town Adana is explained by the Assyrian tables with the Shemite word Nadu. The Assyrians named this place Adana, Nadu. Half of an inscribed limestone tablet from the great temple of the sun in southern Babylonia, in the archaic writing of the oldest known period, mentions the town Adana or Nadu, which is Nod, Genesis 4:16. Nadu was a south Babylonian city. So the city Nimrod built in is the same place Cain resided in: Nadu is Nod, the land of Nod in which the city Enoch was built. Nod is southern Babylon, eastward of the garden of Eden.

“And Cain knew his wife; and she conceived, and bare Enoch: and he builded a city, and called the name of the city, after the name of his son, Enoch.” He resided in the land of Nod and built the city called Enoch, the wicked Enoch, after his son Enoch, the wicked son.

Enoch is the Akkadian Unuk, the place of settlement, the ancient name of Iraq. The city of Enoch built in the land of Nod is Babylon. And the wicked Irad is Eridu, the great port of the Babylonians. They deified Methusael, the Cainite descendant we read in Genesis 4, as the husband of the goddess, with a shrine in the forest of Eridu. So they identified this man as a god.

Enoch is the same as Iraq that Nimrod built on top of. That’s why, when they built that tower, the Lord came there and stopped them and confounded the languages: they gained the same evil wisdom Cain gained in that same area. Their understanding was on another level, a technological level. Nimrod had understanding from his forefather: Cain went over there, and Nimrod went over there and did the same thing Cain did, built the city and gained the same wisdom from the same spirits over there. And what is Esau? The daughter of Babylon. Nothing new.
